questions.source: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy.
questions.prompt: How should the player trigger a punch on PC?

options.label: Left mouse click
options.description: Standard PC combat control: left mouse button throws a punch, matching common Roblox fighting-game conventions.

options.label: Dedicated key (e.g. F)
options.description: A specific keyboard key triggers the punch instead of the mouse, leaving mouse look free during the swing.

options.label: Automatic when in range
options.description: Punching happens automatically on a timer whenever the player stands close to the dummy, with no manual attack input.

questions.recommendationReason: Left-click is the standard, discoverable PC attack control for melee/fighting mechanics and keeps camera control on the mouse's other functions unaffected.

questions.prompt: The selected punch animation pack is built for the R6 character rig. Which character rig should this project use so the animation plays correctly?

options.label: Use R6 characters
options.description: Set the experience to use the classic R6 rig so the selected animation pack plays exactly as authored, with no retargeting needed.

options.label: Keep default R15 characters
options.description: Keep Roblox's default R15 rig; the selected R6 animation would need retargeting or a different R15-compatible punch animation may need to be sourced instead.

questions.recommendationReason: Matching the rig to the already-selected animation avoids retargeting risk and guarantees the punch animation plays as intended.

individual sound clips available to audition and pick from

mechanics.text: Core loop: the player spawns on the existing baseplate a short walk from a single stationary Target Dummy. The player throws a punch with a left mouse click (the confirmed PC attack input), which plays a punching animation on the player's character. The project uses the R6 character rig so the selected punch animation pack plays exactly as authored, with no retargeting needed. If the player is within melee range and roughly facing the dummy when the animation's swing lands, a hit registers: the punch/hit sound plays, and an on-screen counter GUI increments by one. The dummy remains in place and uses its own bundled respawn/hit-reaction behavior (from the selected 'Target Dummy (Respawns)' asset) after being hit; punching continues to function normally after any respawn. A short cooldown equal to roughly the animation's length prevents a single click from registering multiple counter increments. There is no player health, damage trade, or opponent AI — this is a one-sided practice/combat-trainer loop centered on landing repeatable punches and watching the counter climb. The counter is a persistent, always-visible HUD element (not tied to a menu) and is session-only; it does not save between play sessions. Per the confirmed answers, these limits are kept as-is: only one Target Dummy is present (no additional enemies or players), the counter remains session-only with no persistence, the dummy has no gameplay health/death state despite any bundled damage logic (only successful punch contact matters), and no additional opponents, rounds, timers, or win/lose conditions are added.
assumptions: Only one Target Dummy is present; there are no additional enemies or players to fight.
The punch counter is session-only and resets on rejoin; no data persistence is implemented.
A short cooldown matching the punch animation's length prevents duplicate counter increments from a single swing.
Hit registration uses the dummy's existing hit-detection/respawn behavior where possible, falling back to a simple range-and-facing check if the bundled asset does not expose usable hit events.
The dummy does not have a health/death state for gameplay purposes even if its bundled script includes damage logic; only successful punch contact matters for the counter.
No additional opponents, rounds, timers, or win/lose conditions are added since the request describes a single repeatable punching loop.
The attack input binding is left mouse click, the confirmed default PC melee control.
The project uses the R6 character rig, confirmed to match the selected punch animation pack without retargeting.

theme.text: A minimalist, arcade-style combat-training presentation: a plain open training area on the default baseplate with a single practice dummy as the clear focal point. The tone is functional and gym-like rather than narrative — clean HUD typography for the punch counter, a neutral color palette matching the existing sky/lighting, and no added scenery that would distract from the punch-and-count loop. Visual hierarchy: dummy as the only prop of interest, HUD counter as the only persistent UI, both easily readable at a glance.
assumptions: The experience has no narrative framing beyond 'practice your punches on a dummy'; theme is purely a functional training-gym aesthetic.
No additional decorative props (mats, punching bags, posters, ropes) are added since none were requested.

environment.text: Player spawns near the center of the existing baseplate (ground top at y=0), matching the host's default spawn behavior with no added enclosure. A short walk away (roughly 12 studs from spawn), the Target Dummy stands facing the spawn point in an open, unobstructed patch of the baseplate, giving the player a clear, immediate sightline to their objective on arrival. The on-screen punch counter is anchored near the top-center of the screen so it stays visible while the player faces and punches the dummy. First minute: the player spawns, immediately sees the dummy a few steps ahead, walks up, throws a punch (animation plays), hears the impact sound and watches the counter tick from 0 to 1, then repeats punches to keep increasing the counter — the visible, climbing counter is the immediate reason to keep punching. No walls, ceiling, or raised platform are added since the request does not call for an enclosed arena.
assumptions: Spawn stays at the host-provided default location close to the ground; no custom spawn platform is added.
The dummy is placed within easy walking distance (~12 studs) of spawn so the first-minute loop is immediate.
No arena walls, ropes, or boundary geometry are added since only a punching-dummy loop was requested.

foundation.title: Target Dummy Punch Trainer
foundation.summary: A single-loop PC combat-training experience built directly on the existing baseplate. The player spawns near the default spawn point and immediately sees a stationary Target Dummy (Respawns, asset 112770048) roughly 12 studs away in an open, unobstructed patch. Left mouse click throws a punch: the local character plays a punch swing extracted from the selected R6 fight-animation pack (asset 15008746676, embedded clip key 1/11/1). While the swing is near/facing the dummy, the server validates the hit (reusing the dummy's own bundled hit/respawn scripts where they expose usable signals, else a simple server-side range+facing fallback), plays a punch/hit sound chosen from the Punch Sounds pack (asset 16583762) at the dummy, and increments a persistent, always-visible top-center HUD counter. A short server-enforced cooldown matching the animation length prevents duplicate counts per swing. The dummy keeps its own respawn/hit-reaction behavior; punching continues to work normally after each respawn. There is no player health, opponent AI, multiple dummies, rounds, timers, win/lose state, or save persistence — the counter resets on rejoin by design. Because the animation source is a raw KeyframeSequence inside the pack rather than a published Animation asset, Studio playback uses RegisterKeyframeSequence (temporary ID assigned to Animation.AnimationId); publishing the animation to a live game remains an unresolved limitation to report, not silently bypassed. Because the pack is R6-authored, the project forces the R6 rig per spawning character via a server rig-swap service (Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription), since the global StarterPlayer avatar-type setting lives outside the editable namespace. First minute: player spawns, sees the dummy a few steps ahead, walks up, clicks to punch, sees the animation, hears the impact sound, and watches the HUD counter tick from 0 upward — the climbing counter is the sole, immediate reason to keep punching.
foundation.visualDirection: Minimalist, functional training-gym tone matching the existing default sky/lighting — no lighting changes, no added scenery, no arena walls or ceiling. The Target Dummy is the only visual focal point, standing upright on the baseplate at y=0 facing the spawn point in a clear, open sightline. The HUD is the only persistent UI: a compact, high-contrast counter (bold sans-serif numeral with a small 'Punches' label) anchored top-center, sized to stay readable during motion without obstructing the dummy. No decorative props, mats, or posters are added. Feedback hierarchy on each successful hit: animation swing completes, impact sound fires in sync at the dummy's position, and the HUD number updates immediately after — all three cues land close together so the hit feels singular and readable.

combatInput.title: Target Dummy Punch Trainer
combatInput.summary: A single-loop PC combat-training experience built directly on the existing baseplate. The player spawns near the default spawn point and immediately sees a stationary Target Dummy (Respawns, asset 112770048) roughly 12 studs away in an open, unobstructed patch. Left mouse click throws a punch: the local character plays a punch swing extracted from the selected R6 fight-animation pack (asset 15008746676, embedded clip key 1/11/1). While the swing is near/facing the dummy, the server validates the hit (reusing the dummy's own bundled hit/respawn scripts where they expose usable signals, else a simple server-side range+facing fallback), plays a punch/hit sound chosen from the Punch Sounds pack (asset 16583762) at the dummy, and increments a persistent, always-visible top-center HUD counter. A short server-enforced cooldown matching the animation length prevents duplicate counts per swing. The dummy keeps its own respawn/hit-reaction behavior; punching continues to work normally after each respawn. There is no player health, opponent AI, multiple dummies, rounds, timers, win/lose state, or save persistence — the counter resets on rejoin by design. Because the animation source is a raw KeyframeSequence inside the pack rather than a published Animation asset, Studio playback uses RegisterKeyframeSequence (temporary ID assigned to Animation.AnimationId); publishing the animation to a live game remains an unresolved limitation to report, not silently bypassed. Because the pack is R6-authored, the project forces the R6 rig per spawning character via a server rig-swap service (Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription), since the global StarterPlayer avatar-type setting lives outside the editable namespace. First minute: player spawns, sees the dummy a few steps ahead, walks up, clicks to punch, sees the animation, hears the impact sound, and watches the HUD counter tick from 0 upward — the climbing counter is the sole, immediate reason to keep punching.
combatInput.visualDirection: Minimalist, functional training-gym tone matching the existing default sky/lighting — no lighting changes, no added scenery, no arena walls or ceiling. The Target Dummy is the only visual focal point, standing upright on the baseplate at y=0 facing the spawn point in a clear, open sightline. The HUD is the only persistent UI: a compact, high-contrast counter (bold sans-serif numeral with a small 'Punches' label) anchored top-center, sized to stay readable during motion without obstructing the dummy. No decorative props, mats, or posters are added. Feedback hierarchy on each successful hit: animation swing completes, impact sound fires in sync at the dummy's position, and the HUD number updates immediately after — all three cues land close together so the hit feels singular and readable.

requirements.description: The server is the sole authority deciding whether a punch lands. ServerHitValidator, listening on the PunchRequest RemoteEvent, checks the attacking player's humanoid health, distance to the placed Target Dummy, and facing angle before crediting a hit. The client's local punch animation playback is cosmetic only and never itself confirms a hit or mutates the counter.
requirements.acceptance: Native server-side inspection confirms ServerHitValidator connects PunchRequest.OnServerEvent, reads the sending player's Character/Humanoid.Health, computes distance from the player's root to the dummy and a facing-angle check, and only proceeds to credit a hit when all pass; sending PunchRequest from an out-of-range or non-facing position does not increment the counter.

requirements.description: ServerHitValidator reuses the Target Dummy's own inspected hit/Touched signal from the foundation area's inspection note when one exists, instead of duplicating hit-detection logic; if the foundation inspection found no usable signal, the validator applies the documented server-side range-and-facing fallback check.
requirements.sourceQuote: Hit registration uses the dummy's existing hit-detection/respawn behavior where possible, falling back to a simple range-and-facing check if the bundled asset does not expose usable hit events.
requirements.acceptance: Code comments in ServerHitValidator state which path was taken based on the foundation area's recorded hit-signal inspection note (exact instance path/signal name, or explicit absence), and the implemented validation logic matches that recorded finding rather than assuming one path without checking it.

requirements.description: ServerHitValidator enforces a server-side per-player cooldown, keyed by Player.UserId, approximately equal to the punch animation's length, so a single client punch attempt cannot be credited more than once and rapid or replayed PunchRequest events from one swing do not multiply the counter.
requirements.sourceQuote: A short cooldown equal to roughly the animation's length prevents a single click from registering multiple counter increments.
requirements.acceptance: Native testing shows that firing PunchRequest repeatedly within the cooldown window from the same UserId only credits one hit; a PunchRequest sent after the cooldown window elapses is evaluated normally. The cooldown table is keyed by UserId, not a shared/global value.

requirements.description: PunchCounterState stores each player's validated punch count in a per-player session table indexed by Player.UserId. The stored count and cooldown timestamp are removed when the player leaves (PlayerRemoving), and nothing is written to persistent storage, so the counter resets to zero on rejoin.
requirements.acceptance: Native inspection confirms PunchCounterState keys its count/cooldown tables by Player.UserId, connects Players.PlayerRemoving to delete that player's entry, and contains no DataStore or persistent save calls; simulating a leave-and-rejoin shows the count starts back at zero.

requirements.description: Punch validation continues to function normally through the Target Dummy's own bundled respawn cycle: after the dummy runs its existing respawn/hit-reaction behavior, subsequent PunchRequest events are still evaluated correctly (distance, facing, cooldown, hit-signal reuse or fallback) without errors or a broken state.
requirements.sourceQuote: punching continues to function normally after any respawn.
requirements.acceptance: Native testing across at least one dummy respawn cycle shows ServerHitValidator continues to credit valid hits before and after the dummy's own respawn/hit-reaction script runs, with no script errors and no stuck cooldown or state left over from the respawn.

requirements.description: ServerHitValidator does not implement, read, or depend on any dummy health or death state for crediting a hit, even though the dummy's bundled script may include its own damage logic. Only successful punch contact (via the reused hit signal or the range-and-facing fallback) determines whether the counter increments; the dummy is never destroyed, disabled, or marked dead by this validator.
requirements.acceptance: Native code review of ServerHitValidator confirms it never reads or writes a Health/Died value on the dummy and never calls any destroy/respawn logic itself; a punch is credited purely from the hit-signal/range-facing check regardless of any health value the dummy's own bundled script may be tracking internally.

requirements.description: On each server-validated hit, ServerHitValidator increments the player's count in PunchCounterState and exposes a clear hand-off (an exported BindableEvent/Signal or callback on PunchCounterState/ServerHitValidator) that the hitFeedback area's HitFeedbackService can subscribe to for playing the impact sound and firing PunchResult to the client. ServerHitValidator itself does not play the hit sound or fire PunchResult directly, keeping that ownership with the hitFeedback area per the shared contract.
requirements.acceptance: Native inspection shows PunchCounterState (or ServerHitValidator) exposes a documented signal/function (e.g. OnHitValidated:Fire(player, count)) invoked exactly once per credited hit, and that neither script directly plays a Sound instance or fires the PunchResult RemoteEvent; those actions are left for a downstream subscriber.

nodes.name: PunchInputController
nodes.purpose: Detects left mouse click, applies a client-side cooldown gate matching the animation length, plays the punch animation locally for instant feedback, and forwards the attempt to the server.

nodes.name: PunchAnimationPlayer
nodes.purpose: Loads the R6 punch clip via Animator on the local character and plays it on each triggered punch, exposing its length for cooldown timing.

nodes.name: CharacterRigService
nodes.purpose: Forces the R6 rig on every spawning character (Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription) since the global StarterPlayer avatar-type setting is outside the editable namespace, so the punch clip plays without retargeting.

nodes.name: CombatRemotes
nodes.purpose: Defines the PunchRequest and PunchResult RemoteEvent payload contracts shared between the client input/animation layer and the server hit validator.

nodes.name: ServerHitValidator
nodes.purpose: Validates each PunchRequest against distance, facing angle toward the dummy, character health and a per-player cooldown before deciding whether the swing lands.

nodes.name: TargetDummyRig
nodes.purpose: The placed 'Target Dummy (Respawns)' asset instance with its own bundled hit-reaction and respawn scripts; supplies the target position/part and continues its own respawn cycle after being hit.

nodes.name: HitFeedbackService
nodes.purpose: On a validated hit, plays the selected punch/hit Sound parented at the dummy and notifies the attacking client with the updated session hit count.

nodes.name: PunchCounterState
nodes.purpose: Tracks each player's session-only hit count keyed by UserId, incrementing on validated hits and clearing on leave; never persisted between sessions.

nodes.name: PunchCounterHUD
nodes.purpose: Persistent, always-visible top-center counter ScreenGui that listens for PunchResult and updates the displayed count, rebinding cleanly on CharacterAdded without duplicating HUD instances.

outline.assetStrategy: Target Dummy (Respawns, 112770048): place the model as-is on the baseplate ~12 studs from spawn, upright, unresized; keep its bundled respawn/hit-reaction scripts intact and inspect them first for a usable hit/Touched signal before adding any fallback range+facing check, so behavior is not duplicated. Fighting animation (15008746676, embedded clip key 1/11/1): the punch clip is a raw KeyframeSequence, not a published Animation asset — load it in Studio via RegisterKeyframeSequence and assign the returned ID unchanged to an Animation.AnimationId for Animator playback; report the recorded publishing limitation rather than treating it as blocking Studio integration or inventing a published ID. Punch Sounds (16583762): the pack holds multiple clips — audition them natively and select one clean impact sound, then deliver it to ReplicatedStorage and play it through a Sound parented at the dummy on confirmed hits. R6 rig requirement: since StarterPlayer's global avatar-type property sits outside the editable namespace, a server-side rig service rebuilds each spawning character as R6 via Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription so the animation plays without retargeting.
outline.sharedContracts: RemoteEvents (ReplicatedStorage/Forge_.../Combat): PunchRequest (client->server, no payload beyond the implicit sender) and PunchResult (server->client, payload {hit:boolean, count:number}). Server authority: ServerHitValidator is the sole decider of a landed punch, checking humanoid health, distance to the dummy, facing angle, and a per-player cooldown (~animation length) before crediting a hit; the client's local animation playback is cosmetic only and never itself confirms a hit. Per-player session state (cooldown timestamp, hit count) is keyed by Player.UserId in a server table, cleared on PlayerRemoving; nothing persists across sessions. The Target Dummy retains its own bundled respawn/hit-reaction scripts unmodified; the validator treats those as read-only signals/state, never overriding the dummy's health or death logic since only punch contact (not damage) matters. PunchCounterHUD lives in a persistent ScreenGui (StarterGui or StarterPlayerScripts-managed, ResetOnSpawn=false) that rebinds its display update on every CharacterAdded and disconnects prior connections to avoid duplicate HUD instances. CharacterRigService applies R6 on CharacterAdded before any animation load is attempted, so PunchAnimationPlayer must wait for the rig-service signal (or an R6 Humanoid) before calling Animator:LoadAnimation.

areas.objective: Place the Target Dummy (Respawns, 112770048) upright on the baseplate ~12 studs from spawn facing the spawn point, without resizing or stripping its bundled scripts. Create the CombatRemotes module/RemoteEvents (PunchRequest, PunchResult) in ReplicatedStorage under the namespace. Implement the CharacterRigService on the server to force R6 on every spawning character via Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription, given StarterPlayer's global avatar setting is outside the editable namespace. Scaffold the persistent PunchCounterHUD ScreenGui structure (top-center counter frame, ResetOnSpawn=false) without wiring live data yet. Inspect the Target Dummy's embedded scripts and record whether they expose a usable hit/Touched signal for downstream reuse.

areas.objective: Implement the client-side PunchInputController bound to left mouse click, gated by a local cooldown approximating the animation length. Extract the punch swing clip from the R6 fight-animation pack (15008746676, embedded key 1/11/1) as a KeyframeSequence, register it via RegisterKeyframeSequence, and play it through PunchAnimationPlayer on the local R6 character (waiting on CharacterRigService's R6 rig) each time input fires. Fire PunchRequest to the server after the local gate passes. Report the recorded animation publishing limitation explicitly rather than substituting a different clip.

areas.title: Server Hit Validation
areas.objective: Implement ServerHitValidator listening on PunchRequest: verify the attacking player's humanoid health, distance to the placed dummy, facing angle, and a server-side per-player cooldown (keyed by UserId, cleared on PlayerRemoving) matching the animation length. Reuse the dummy's inspected hit/Touched signal if one was found in the foundation area; otherwise apply the documented range+facing fallback. On a validated hit, update PunchCounterState's per-player session count and hand off to hit feedback. Confirm punching continues to function normally through the dummy's own respawn cycle.

areas.title: Hit Sound and HUD Counter
areas.objective: Audition the Punch Sounds pack (16583762), select one clean impact clip, and deliver it to ReplicatedStorage. Implement HitFeedbackService to play that Sound parented at the dummy synchronized with each server-validated hit, then FireClient PunchResult with {hit:true, count}. Wire PunchCounterHUD to PunchResult.OnClientEvent to update the displayed number immediately, rebinding cleanly on every CharacterAdded so no duplicate HUD instance appears after respawn.
